messages:
emily: Heads up quick design check: I'm iterating on the run-history row for action invocations. Idea: show a tiny inline "diff summary" chip when the action's output schema differs from the expected schema, and let users 'replay' the invocation or open the full schema diff. Need accessibility/copy thoughts.

raj: Love it. Two quick UX constraints: 1) make it visually compact for dense timelines; 2) the replay affordance should be obvious but not noisy. Maybe icon-only for replay with tooltip.

nicole: Accessibility: icon-only buttons must have aria-labels. For the diff chip, include an explicit textual label like "Schema changed" and a short explanation on expand. Also add keyboard focus states.

joel: From eng: replay will call the stored request + environment. We should warn if the original run used a fallback model. Maybe add a confirmation modal with a short summary: model used, truncated input, and "Run again" button.

emily: Good point. For copy: initial chip text options: "Schema changed", "Output mismatch", "Field-level changes". Which is clearest?

aria: "Schema changed" is plain and easy to scan. For announcement (screen readers) use: "Schema changed  3 fields differ. Press Enter to expand details."

nicole: That verboseness for screen readers is perfect. Also, put the count of changed fields in the chip like "Schema changed (3)". Visual numerics help sighted users scan.

raj: Slight concern about noise: if lots of runs show (1) or (2), it could be distracting. Consider an opt-in filter: "Show only runs with schema changes" and a per-user collapse default.

emily: Agree, add a header-level filter and a per-user setting. Also thinking about the expanded diff UX: show a compact table: field | expected type | actual type | sample value. And a `Show JSON` toggle underneath.

joel: Table is fine. Dev perf note: sample value extraction could be expensive for large payloads. Lazy-load the samples after expansion, show skeleton first.

aria: Accessibility detail: when expanding the diff, focus should move into the diff container and the container should be keyboard-trap friendly until user presses Escape or a close button. Also announce via aria-live: "Showing schema diff for action X".

nicole: UX copy for the modal/replay confirmation: Title: "Replay action invocation"; body: "This will re-run the original request using the recorded inputs and the current routing policy. Confirm?" Buttons: "Cancel" / "Replay". Add link text "View request details" inside modal.

emily: One more copy thought: avoid the term "re-run" in product copy  we use "replay" elsewhere. Use "Replay" consistently.

raj: Also telemetry: track replay clicks, confirm:replay ratio, and whether replayed runs still trigger schema diffs. Use that to see if schema drift is transient.

joel: For rollback feature: if replay fails, we could surface a quick "Open rollback suggestion" that links to the schema editor with an autogenerated patch (+/- types) suggestion. That might be ambitious but useful.

aria: For screen readers, when a replay modal opens, announce: "Replay dialog open. Press Escape to cancel." Ensure modal has role=dialog and aria-modal=true.

nicole: Copy alternatives for the chip (short): "Schema  changed", "Mismatch (3)", "Diff: 3". Prefer two-word max. "Schema changed (3)" feels best.

emily: Great. Another tiny visual: color-code the chip (yellow for partial mismatch, red if invocation failed). But don't rely solely on color  add an icon and the number.

raj: Keyboard nav proposal: Tab reaches the chip, Enter expands, Shift+R opens replay modal. Document the shortcut in the header keyboard help.

joel: We'll implement modifier-key guard (Shift+R) server-side too to prevent accidental replays.

emily: Final checklist for mock: 
- Chip states: green/none, yellow (schema changed), red (failed)
- Chip content: icon + text "Schema changed (n)"
- Expand shows compact table + "Show JSON" toggle
- Replay action: icon-only with tooltip + confirmation modal (title, 2 buttons, link to details)
- Lazy-load samples; skeleton UI while loading
- Keyboard: Tab, Enter to expand; Shift+R to replay (with confirmation)
- Accessibility: aria-labels, aria-live announcements, focus trap in dialog, role=dialog, aria-modal, descriptive tooltip via aria-describedby

aria: I'll add the aria attributes to the spec and run a quick VoiceOver/NVDA pass.

nicole: I'll write the concise copy variants for the UI and supply microcopy for tooltips and modal.

emily: Thanks  I'll post the Figma link when the mock is ready and include the annotated accessibility checklist. :sparkles:

ux-bot: Mock uploaded: https://figma.redwood.com/file/xyz/run-history-diff-chip (comment "@emily please annotate keyboard shortcuts")
